prompts.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes or contributed to group efforts over time.

Every person has a creative side, and it can be expressed in many ways: problem solving, original and innovative thinking, and artistically, to name a few. Describe how you express your creative side.
What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
Describe how you have taken advantage of a significant educational opportunity or worked to overcome an educational barrier you have faced.
Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge. How has this challenge affected your academic achievement?
Think about an academic subject that inspires you. Describe how you have furthered this interest inside and/or outside of the classroom.
What have you done to make your school or your community a better place?
Beyond what has already been shared in your application, what do you believe makes you a strong candidate for admissions to the University of California?

intl_finance.document: I-20/DS-2019 application form (electronic link emailed by Admissions) with proof of finances for one academic year (liquid bank statement or bank letter in the student's or a sponsor's name, or a UCR/external sponsor letter) and a passport copy
intl_finance.notes: UCR's new-student FAQ says you may complete the I-20 application and attach all documents even before you are admitted and need not wait for the SIR, but the I-20 is issued once you are admitted. Bank documents: liquid funds, preferably dated within the last 3 months (UCR says it will accept older), official statement or letter with account type, bank name and branch (no screenshots), English, account holder name, and the current available amount (not an average) with currency. A sponsor cannot be in F-1 or J-1 status. The verification amounts are on the I-20 request form and may change; no date is published.

notes: The 8 Personal Insight Questions are the same for all UC campuses (answer 4, max 350 words each); text copied from the UC Admissions page (source 1), which does not print a cycle year. Source 2 (UC counselor guide titled 2026-27) confirms the same format for the 2026-27 application: respond to 4 of the 8 questions, 350 words maximum per response. The UC application also has optional Additional comments boxes (source 2); they are not essay prompts and are not listed here. Source 5 (UCR international admissions) tells first-year applicants to answer four out of eight personal insight questions and lists no other written questions. In intl_finance, source 3 is the main one; source 4 is the FAQ on timing and sponsors. The when value is set to after_admission because the I-20 is issued after admission, even though submission before admission is allowed.
